SUPPLEMENTAL JOB DISPLACEMENT BENEFIT (WORKERS' COMP VOUCHER) — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

SUPPLEMENTAL JOB DISPLACEMENT BENEFIT — OVERVIEW
This information sheet describes the Supplemental Job Displacement Benefit (SJDB) available under California workers' compensation law, Labor Code § 4658.7. It concerns Jordan Lee's work injury at Acme, Inc. with a reported injury date of October 1, 2026 (lower back strain from lifting). The SJDB is a voucher for retraining or skill enhancement that may become available to a worker who has sustained permanent partial disability from a work injury and whom the employer does not offer, or who does not receive a qualifying offer of, regular, modified, or alternative work. This sheet states the general provisions of the law; it does not determine whether any particular worker qualifies for the benefit, and it is not a claim form, a voucher, or a substitute for the notices and forms that the workers' compensation claims administrator is separately required to provide.

ELIGIBILITY TRIGGER: PERMANENT PARTIAL DISABILITY AND NO QUALIFYING RETURN-TO-WORK OFFER
Under Labor Code § 4658.7, applicable to injuries occurring on or after January 1, 2013, a worker whose work injury causes permanent partial disability is entitled to a Supplemental Job Displacement Benefit unless the employer makes a qualifying offer of regular, modified, or alternative work as defined in Labor Code § 4658.1. To be qualifying, the offer must (1) be made no later than 60 days after the claims administrator receives the first report from the primary treating physician, an agreed medical evaluator, or a qualified medical evaluator finding the disability permanent and stationary and that it has caused permanent partial disability, and (2) be for regular, modified, or alternative work lasting at least 12 months. An offer that is not timely made, that does not last at least 12 months, or that the employer never makes at all does not defeat entitlement to the benefit.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "If the injury causes permanent partial disability, the injured employee shall be entitled to a supplemental job displacement benefit as provided in this section unless the employer makes an offer of regular, modified, or alternative work, as defined in Section 4658.1, that meets both of the following criteria"
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(a)-(b), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  "The offer is for regular work, modified work, or alternative work lasting at least 12 months."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(b)(1)-(2), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  "This section shall apply to injuries occurring on or after January 1, 2013."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(a), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  Known gap: This statute defines the SJDB voucher trigger but incorporates by reference the separate definitions of 'regular work,' 'modified work,' and 'alternative work' in Labor Code § 4658.1, which are not reproduced here. Whether a specific job offer meets those definitions, whether an offer was actually timely under the 60-day period, and whether an employee's PD rating in a specific claim is in fact 'permanent partial' (as opposed to permanent total, or not yet permanent and stationary) are factual and medical determinations for the workers' compensation claims process, not something this sheet can resolve.

TIMING OF THE RETURN-TO-WORK OFFER AND THE VOUCHER OFFER
The 60-day period for a qualifying offer of regular, modified, or alternative work runs from the claims administrator's receipt of the first physician report finding the worker's disability permanent and stationary and permanently partially disabling. If no qualifying offer is made within that 60-day period, Labor Code § 4658.7(c) requires that the Supplemental Job Displacement Benefit itself be offered to the employee within 20 days after that 60-day period expires.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The offer is made no later than 60 days after receipt by the claims administrator of the first report received from either the primary treating physician, an agreed medical evaluator, or a qualified medical evaluator, in the form created by the administrative director pursuant to subdivision (h), finding that the disability from all conditions for which compensation is claimed has become permanent and stationary and that the injury has caused permanent partial disability."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(b)(1), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  "The supplemental job displacement benefit shall be offered to the employee within 20 days after the expiration of the time for making an offer of regular, modified, or alternative work pursuant to paragraph (1) of subdivision (b)."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(c), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  Known gap: The statute measures the 60-day period from the claims administrator's receipt of a qualifying physician report, an event this sheet cannot independently verify or calendar; the precise date that period began, and whether the 20-day voucher-offer deadline was met, depend on claims-file records outside this document.

VOUCHER VALUE AND PERMITTED USES
The Supplemental Job Displacement Benefit takes the form of a voucher currently redeemable up to an aggregate of $6,000 per Labor Code § 4658.7(d). The voucher may be applied, at the injured employee's choice, to: education-related retraining or skill enhancement (including tuition, fees, books, and other required expenses) at a California public school or a provider certified on the state's Eligible Training Provider List; occupational licensing or professional certification fees, related examination fees, and examination preparation course fees; the services of licensed placement agencies, vocational or return-to-work counseling, and résumé preparation (together capped at 10 percent of the voucher amount); tools required by an enrolled training or educational program; computer equipment, up to $1,000; and up to $500 as a miscellaneous expense reimbursement or advance payable without itemized documentation. The statute expressly excludes voucher payment for transportation, travel expenses, telephone or internet access, clothing or uniforms, or other incidental expenses beyond that $500 miscellaneous allowance.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The supplemental job displacement benefit shall be in the form of a voucher redeemable as provided in this section up to an aggregate of six thousand dollars ($6,000)."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(d), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  "Payment for education-related retraining or skill enhancement, or both, at a California public school or with a provider that is certified and on the state’s Eligible Training Provider List (EPTL), as authorized by the federal Workforce Investment Act (P.L. 105-220), including payment of tuition, fees, books, and other expenses required by the school for retraining or skill enhancement."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(e)(1), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  "Payment for the services of licensed placement agencies, vocational or return-to-work counseling, and résumé preparation, all up to a combined limit of 10 percent of the amount of the voucher."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(e)(3), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  "Up to five hundred dollars ($500) as a miscellaneous expense reimbursement or advance, payable upon request and without need for itemized documentation or accounting. The employee shall not be entitled to any other voucher payment for transportation, travel expenses, telephone or Internet access, clothing or uniforms, or incidental expenses."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(e)(6), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  Known gap: The $6,000 aggregate figure and the sub-limits described here are the amounts currently codified in the text of Labor Code § 4658.7 as verified directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov on the date checked above; this figure has been changed by the Legislature before (the pre-2013 version of this benefit used a different, PD-rating-tiered schedule) and could be amended again, so the amount should be confirmed against the current statute at the time of use rather than assumed from this sheet indefinitely.

VOUCHER EXPIRATION
Under Labor Code § 4658.7(f), the voucher expires two years after the date it is furnished to the employee, or five years after the date of injury, whichever is later. To be reimbursed, expenses must be incurred and submitted to the employer with appropriate documentation before that expiration date; the statute states there is no entitlement to payment or reimbursement of expenses not incurred and documented in time.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The voucher shall expire two years after the date the voucher is furnished to the employee, or five years after the date of injury, whichever is later."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(f), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  "The employee shall not be entitled to payment or reimbursement of any expenses that have not been incurred and submitted with appropriate documentation to the employer prior to the expiration date."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(f), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  Known gap: Because the deadline runs from whichever furnishing date and injury date apply to the specific claim, and 'the date of injury' for a cumulative-trauma or multiple-incident claim can itself be a disputed determination in workers' compensation practice, this sheet cannot calculate a specific expiration date for any individual worker's voucher.

RESTRICTION ON SETTLEMENT OF THE BENEFIT; EMPLOYER LIABILITY WHILE USING THE VOUCHER
Labor Code § 4658.7(g) prohibits settlement or commutation of a claim for the Supplemental Job Displacement Benefit under the Chapter 2 (compromise and release, commencing with Section 5000) or Chapter 3 (commutation, commencing with Section 5100) procedures of Part 3 of the Labor Code's workers' compensation provisions. Separately, Labor Code § 4658.7(i) provides that an employer is not liable for compensation for injuries incurred by the employee while using the voucher.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Settlement or commutation of a claim for the supplemental job displacement benefit shall not be permitted under Chapter 2 (commencing with Section 5000) or Chapter 3 (commencing with Section 5100) of Part 3."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(g), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  "An employer shall not be liable for compensation for injuries incurred by the employee while utilizing the voucher."
  — Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7(i), Cal. Lab. Code § 4658.7 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=4658.7.)
  Known gap: This statute bars settlement of the SJDB claim specifically under the two named chapters; it does not address, and this sheet does not opine on, how a broader workers' compensation compromise and release agreement that references or lists the SJDB voucher as a settled item may be interpreted, which is a matter of case-specific contract and settlement-agreement construction.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF RECEIPT OF INFORMATION
This information sheet regarding the Supplemental Job Displacement Benefit was provided to Jordan Lee by Acme, Inc. on September 1, 2026 in Oakland, California. Signing below acknowledges receipt of this information sheet only; it does not waive, establish, or resolve any entitlement to the Supplemental Job Displacement Benefit or any other workers' compensation benefit.
